/-!
# Digit $2$ in base $3$ representation of $2^n$

*References:*
- [Some Unconventional Problems in Number Theory](https://doi.org/10.2307/2689842)
  by *Paul Erdös*, Mathematics Magazine 52, no. 2, p. 67, 1979
- [arxiv/2107.12475](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.12475)
  **Hardness of busy beaver value BB(15)** by *Tristan Stérin, Damien Woods*
- [Hardness of Busy Beaver Value BB(15)](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-72621-7_9)
  by *Tristan Stérin, Damien Woods*, Reachability Problems, Lecture Notes in Computer Science
  15050, Springer, Cham (2024)
-/

namespace Arxiv.«2107.12475»

/--
For $n > 8$, $2^n$ is not the the sum of distinct powers of $3$. Expressed here in terms of the base $3$ digits of $n$.

This conjecture is equivalent to the halting of a $15$-state $2$-symbol Turing Machine.

TODO(lezeau): Formalize the Turing Machine version of this problem.

Source: *Hardness of Busy Beaver Value BB(15)*: https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-031-72621-7_9
This is also https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.12475.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem CollatzLike (n : ℕ) (hn : 8 < n) : 2 ∈ Nat.digits 3 (2^n) := by
  sorry

/--
For $n = 8$, $2$ is not contained in the base $3$ digits of $n$.
-/
@[category test, AMS 5 11]
theorem two_not_in_digits_three_pow_eight : 2 ∉ Nat.digits 3 (2^8) := by norm_num

end Arxiv.«2107.12475»

findings.description: The docstring says the conjecture is equivalent to the halting of a 15-state, 2-symbol Turing machine. This reverses the cited result: the constructed machine halts exactly when the conjecture is false, so the universally quantified Lean conjecture corresponds to non-halting. The Lean theorem itself has the correct polarity.
findings.source_evidence: Stérin–Woods, arXiv:2107.12475v2, Theorem 1: “There is an explicit 15-state 2-symbol Turing machine that halts if and only if Erdős' conjecture is false.” Section 2 specifies execution from an all-blank tape. The published abstract states the same equivalence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.12475 and https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-72621-7_9.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the docstring to say that the conjecture is equivalent to non-halting, on blank tape, of the explicit 15-state, 2-symbol machine constructed in the paper. Leave the Lean theorem unchanged.

findings.description: The final sentence of the first docstring paragraph says the formulation uses the base-3 digits of n, whereas the Lean statement correctly uses Nat.digits 3 (2^n). These are different quantities: for example, n = 9 satisfies the hypothesis but 9 = 100₃ has no digit 2, while 2^9 does contain a ternary digit 2. Both facts were verified in Lean.
findings.source_evidence: Conjecture 1 of arXiv:2107.12475v2 says: “For all natural numbers n > 8 there is at least one digit 2 in the base 3 representation of 2^n.” https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.12475. Erdős' original formulation concerns 2^k, not k, in Mathematics Magazine 52 (1979), p. 67: https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1979-22.pdf.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace “the base $3$ digits of $n$” with “the base $3$ digits of $2^n$”.

findings.description: The docstring asserts that at n = 8, the base-3 digits of n omit 2. Literally this is false, since 8 = 22₃. The proved Lean statement correctly concerns 2^8 = 256 = 100111₃. Lean checks confirmed Nat.digits 3 8 = [2, 2] and Nat.digits 3 (2^8) = [1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 1].
findings.source_evidence: Stérin–Woods, arXiv:2107.12475v2, §1.2 explicitly lists 256 with ternary representation 100111 as a known exception. Erdős, Mathematics Magazine 52 (1979), p. 67, writes “However, 2^8 = 256 = 3^5 + 3^2 + 3 + 1.” https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1979-22.pdf.
findings.suggested_fix: Say “For $n = 8$, $2$ is not contained in the base $3$ digits of $2^n$”, or state directly that the ternary expansion of $2^8$ omits $2$. Leave the proved theorem unchanged.

reformulations.difference: Erdős' original article states that 2^n is not a sum of distinct powers of 3 for n > 8; Lean states that the ternary digit list of 2^n contains 2. The arXiv paper also explicitly uses this digit formulation.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every ternary digit is 0, 1, or 2. Omitting 2 means that the number is the finite sum of 3^i over exactly the positions whose digit is 1, with distinct nonnegative exponents. Conversely, a finite sum of distinct powers of 3 has coefficients only 0 or 1, hence no carries and no ternary digit 2, by uniqueness of positional expansion. Negating gives precisely the Lean statement for each n > 8. Little-endian ordering in Nat.digits does not affect membership.

sources_consulted: Paul Erdős, Some Unconventional Problems in Number Theory, Mathematics Magazine 52(2) (1979), 67–70, especially p. 67; original article read through its embedded PDF text at https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1979-22.pdf (DOI: 10.2307/2689842).

https://arxiv.org/e-print/2107.12475 (redirected to https://arxiv.org/src/2107.12475) — LaTeX source, especially Conjecture 1, Theorem 1, §1.2, and the machine-halting proof.
